Rashi on Bava Kamma 37a:12:1.hebrew: השתא יש לומר מקטנים לקטנים - כגון ממינו לשאינו מינו, אשמעינן רישא אינו מועד; מקטנים לגדולים מבעיא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 37a:12:1.english: Now it can be said, from small [animals] to small [animals] - For example, from its own species to a different species, the first clause [of the Mishnah] teaches us [that] it is not forewarned; [then] from small [animals] to large [animals], is it necessary [to state]?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 37a:14:1.hebrew: דאפילו מאדם - דאית ליה מזלא, לא הוי סתמיה מועד לבהמה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 37a:14:1.english: That even from a person - who has a guardian angel [mazal], it is not ordinarily [considered] forewarned with regard to an animal.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 37a:15:1.english: But if you say "and it is not forewarned" - [regarding] what is not its own species we learned [in the Mishnah].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 37a:15:2.english: But in an ordinary case it is forewarned - from its own species to [a species] not of its own kind.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 37a:15:3.hebrew: השתא מבהמה לבהמה הוי מועד - ואפי' למין אחר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 37a:15:3.english: Now, from an animal to an animal it is forewarned - And even to another species.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 37a:15:4.hebrew: מאדם לבהמה מבעיא - והא ליכא למימר דהיא גופה אצטריך לאשמועינן, דהיכא דחזינן דאינו מועד לבהמה, אינו משלם על בהמה אלא חצי נזק, דהא פשיטא לן דתם משלם חצי נזק:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 37a:15:4.english: From a person to an animal, is it necessary [to state]? - And one cannot say that it was necessary to teach us this [point] itself — that where we see that it is not forewarned for an animal, he pays only half-damages for an animal — for it is obvious to us that a tam [unwarned ox] pays half-damages.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 37a:16:1.hebrew: רישא אחזרה קאי - והיא גופה אצטריך, דאבהמה לא משלם אלא חצי נזק. ואע"ג דאייעד ליה, הואיל והדר ביה, חזר לתמותו, ואע"ג דלא הדר ביה מאדם:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 37a:16:1.english: The first clause refers to reversion - And that itself was necessary [to teach], that for [goring] an animal he pays only half damages. Even though it had been forewarned regarding it, since it reverted, it has returned to its innocuous status, even though it did not revert regarding humans.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 37a:1:1.hebrew: אין צריכין פרוזבול - דבלאו הכי לא משמט שביעית לחוב שלהן, דאנן ידייהו דיתמי אנן ורמי עלן להפוכי בזכותייהו. הלכך, שטרות שלהן כמסורים לב"ד דמי, ותנן: המוסר שטרותיו לב"ד אין משמיטין, וזהו גופו של פרוזבול: מוסרני לכם פלוני ופלוני הדיינין, במסכת גטין (דף לו.). להכי נקט ר"ג, דנשיא הוה ובית דינו ב"ד חשוב:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 37a:1:1.english: [Orphans] do not require a prosbol - For even without this, the Sabbatical year does not abrogate their debt, since we [the court] are the hand of the orphans, and it is incumbent upon us to act in their favor. Therefore, their [debt] documents are considered as if handed over to the court, and we learned in a Mishnah: "One who hands over his documents to the court, [the Sabbatical year] does not abrogate [his debts]," and this is the essential text of a prosbol: "I hand over to you, so-and-so and so-and-so, the judges," in Tractate Gittin (36a). For this reason [the Gemara] specifically mentions Rabban Gamliel, because he was the Nasi and his court was an important court.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 37a:20:1.hebrew: שיולי משיילי ליה - היכא דחזינן דהועד לשבתות ובימי החול לא נגח, מאי דיניה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 37a:20:1.english: They were asking him - Where we see that [an ox] was forewarned for Shabbatot and on weekdays it did not gore, what is its law?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 37a:20:2.english: And furthermore, what was he responding to them - For they too are saying, "[it] is not forewarned."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 37a:22:1.hebrew: פרושי קא מפרש לה - איידי דנקט לה משום דוקיא דידיה, דדייקינן: הא סתמא הוי מועד — על כרחיך אסקיה למילתיה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 37a:22:1.english: It is explaining it - Since [the Tanna] stated it because of its inference — that we infer: "but [in an] unspecified [case], it is forewarned" — [he] perforce concluded his statement.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 37a:23:1.hebrew: אלא אי אמרת אינו מועד תנן פסקה - למילתיה ואשמועינן דאינו מועד, מאי תו דקתני למי שאינו מועד כו':
Rashi on Bava Kamma 37a:23:1.english: But if you say we learned "it is not forewarned," it concluded - its statement and taught us that it is not forewarned; [then] what [need is there] further for it to teach "for one with regard to which it is not forewarned," etc.?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 37a:23:2.english: Until now, etc. - [This is stated] as a rhetorical question.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 37a:24:1.english: And if you say [that] Rav Pappa's [opinion] is also [accepted] - that ordinarily, it is not forewarned for [a species] not of its own kind.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 37a:24:2.hebrew: נגח שור וחמור וגמל נעשה מועד לכל - ולא בעינן ג' נגיחות לכל חד וחד, מאחר שנתקיימה העדאתו ע"י ג' מינין:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 37a:24:2.english: [If it] gored an ox, a donkey, and a camel, it is rendered forewarned for all - And we do not require three gorings for each and every one, since its forewarning was established through three species.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 37a:25:1.hebrew: לסירוגין - אם יגח רצופין, אינו משלם אלא חצי נזק על האחרון:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 37a:25:1.english: Alternately - If it gores [oxen] consecutively, [the owner] pays only half-damages for the latter [one].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 37a:3:1.english: A worn zuz - Its image is diminished.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 37a:3:2.english: And it was not taken from him - He was unable to spend it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 37a:5:1.english: Behold, it is forewarned for Shabbatot - Because it is idle from work and its mind becomes haughty.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 37a:5:2.hebrew: ואינו מועד לימות החול - מה משפטו של זה? תלמידיו היו שואלין אותו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 37a:5:2.english: And is not forewarned for weekdays - What is the law of this [ox]? His students were asking him.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 37a:6:1.hebrew: ג' ימי שבתות - לאחר שהועד לשבתות, העבירו לפניו שוורים בג' שבתות ולא נגח, חזר לתמותו. ואם חזר ונגח, אין משלם אלא חצי נזק:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 37a:6:1.english: Three days of Shabbat - After it was forewarned with regard to Shabbats, [if] they passed oxen before it on three Shabbats and it did not gore, it returns to its innocuous status. And if it gores again, [the owner] pays only half-damages.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 37a:7:1.hebrew: ואינו מועד תנן - ואין מועד לשאינו מינו, דידעינן ביה דלא נגח, וכגון דעברינהו להו קמיה ולא נגח. הלכך, למי שאינו מועד לו, אם נגחו אחר זמן משלם חצי נזק; אבל מסתמא, אם הועד לזה מועד אף לזה, וכן אם הועד לקטנים מועד לגדולים:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 37a:7:1.english: And it is not forewarned [is what] we learned - [That is,] it is not forewarned for a species other than its own, where we know about it that it does not gore [them] — such as where they passed them before it and it did not gore. Therefore, for that [species] to which it is not forewarned, if it gores it later on, [the owner] pays half-damages; but ordinarily, if it was forewarned for this [species], it is forewarned for that [species] as well, and similarly, if it was forewarned for small [animals], it is forewarned for large [animals].

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 37a:1:1.hebrew: אין צריכין פרוזבול - דשטרות שלהם דמי כמסורין לב"ד, כך פירש בקונטרס. וא"ת: מלוה על פה מאי איכא למימר, דכותבין עליה פרוזבול כדמוכח בהשולח (גיטין דף לו.)? וי"ל: דהוי כאילו החוב שלהם מסור לב"ד; ואפי' אין ללוה קרקע, מקנים לו חכמים קרקע בשביל תקנת היתומים, שאין כותבין פרוזבול אלא על הקרקע:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 37a:1:1.english: They do not require a prosbol - For their promissory notes are considered as if handed over to the court — so Rashi [lit., the Kuntres] explained. And if you ask: What is there to say regarding an oral loan, for which one writes a prosbol, as is proven in [the chapter] HaSholeach (Gittin 36a)? One can answer that it is as if their debt is handed over to the court; and even if the borrower has no land, the Sages grant him land for the sake of the enactment [on behalf] of the orphans, for one only writes a prosbol upon land.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 37a:25:1.hebrew: שור ולא נגח - בתרא דנקט, כדי שאם יגח לאלתר, משלם נ"ש:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 37a:25:1.english: An ox and [it] did not gore - [The reason] that [the Baraita] stated the final [instance is] so that if it gores immediately [afterward], it pays full damages.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 37a:25:2.hebrew: נעשה מועד לסירוגין לשוורים - וא"ת: לרב זביד, אפי' לכל דבר הוי מועד? וי"ל: כגון שראה שאר בהמות ולא נגחן:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 37a:25:2.english: It is rendered forewarned with regard to alternate oxen - And if you ask: According to Rav Zevid, it is forewarned even for everything? And one can answer: [It refers to a case] such as where it saw other animals and did not gore them.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 37a:26:1.hebrew: נעשה מועד לסירוגין לכל - ע"כ בשלא ראה בינתיים כלום, דאי ראה לא הוי מועד [לכל] לסירוגין. וא"ת: כיון שלא ראה אחרים, לשוורים לחודיה הוי מועד לכל לסירוגין לרב זביד? וי"ל: דקסבר רב זביד דרבותא קמ"ל, דס"ד בהנך מיני דחזא ולא נגח לא הוי מועד, ולאו בסירוגין תליא מלתא. א"נ: בשעה שנגח ג' מינים הללו היו לפניו מינים הרבה, ולא נגח אלא אלו; דהשתא אם היו שלשתן שוורים, הייתי אומר: כיון דכל שעה מזומן ליגח השוורים ומניח שאר מינים, אין מועד ליגח אלא שוורים; אבל השתא דהוו ג' מינים, האחד מהם נוגח ואינו חושש ליגח אלא האחד:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 37a:26:1.english: It is rendered forewarned with regard to alternate [animals of] all [species] - Perforce, [this is] where it did not see anything in between, for if it did see [other animals], it would not be rendered forewarned [for all] alternately. And if you ask: Since it did not see others, [even] with oxen alone it would [already] be rendered forewarned for all alternately according to Rav Zevid? One can answer: Rav Zevid holds that [the baraita] teaches us a novelty, for it might have entered your mind [to think] that regarding those species that it saw and did not gore, it is not forewarned, and the matter does not depend on alternation. Alternatively: At the time it gored these three species, there were many species before it, and it gored only these; for now, if all three of them had been oxen, I would have said that since it is constantly ready to gore oxen and leaves the other species alone, it is only forewarned to gore oxen; but now that they are three [different] species, it gores one of them and is only concerned to gore that one.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 37a:5:1.hebrew: הרי הוא מועד לשבתות - מפרש בירושלמי: לפי שראה אותם במלבושים נאים אחרים, וחשובים בעיניו נכרים ואינו מכירם:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 37a:5:1.english: "Behold, it is forewarned with regard to Shabbatot" - [It] explains in the Jerusalem Talmud: because it saw them in different, fine garments, and they are considered strangers in its eyes, and it does not recognize them.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 37a:6:1.hebrew: משיחזור בו ג' שבתות - אע"ג דכבר אשמועינן רבי יהודה בפ"ב (דף כג:), אצטריך; דס"ד, הואיל ולאו מועד אלא לשבתות, לא בעי חזרה כ"כ. ולפ"ה ניחא, דמפרש מועד לשבתות לפי שאין עושה מלאכה, דקמ"ל דאפי' שבת ממלאכה בימי החול ולא נגח, לא הוי חזרה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 37a:6:1.english: When it reverts [for] three Shabbatot - Even though Rabbi Yehudah already taught us [the three-time reversion rule] in the second chapter (23b), [this teaching] is necessary; for one might have thought [that] since it is only forewarned for Shabbatot, it does not require so much of a reversion. And according to Rashi's commentary it is [even more] understandable, since he explains [that it is] forewarned for Shabbatot because it does not perform work [then], for [this baraita] teaches us that even if it rested from work on weekdays and did not gore, that is not [considered] a reversion.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 37a:7:1.hebrew: רב זביד אמר ואינו מועד תנן - הא סתמא הוי מועד לשאין מינו. ואפילו מבהמה לאדם נמי שמעי' לה לקמן בפירקין (בבא קמא דף מא.), דסתמא הוי מועד, גבי הא דפריך: "וכי מאחר דמתם קטלינן ליה, מועד היכי משכחת לה?", ומפרש רב זביד: כגון שהרג ג' בהמות. והוה מצי למיתני במתני': "מועד לבהמה ואינו מועד לאדם", לאשמועינן דסתמא הוי מועד. ומיהו שמא חזר בו רב זביד מההיא דלקמן, כדפריך עלה התם, שאם לא תאמר כן, קשי' ליה ההיא דריש מכילתין (דף ב:):
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 37a:7:1.english: Rav Zevid said: We learned [in the Mishnah] "and it is not forewarned" - Thus, by default, it is forewarned for other species. And even from an animal to a human we also learn this later in our chapter (Bava Kamma 41a), that by default it is forewarned, regarding that which [the Gemara] asks: "Since we put it to death even when it is innocuous, how can you find a case of a forewarned [ox]?" And Rav Zevid explains: For example, where it killed three animals. And [the Tanna] could have taught in the Mishnah: "forewarned for an animal and not forewarned for a human," to teach us that by default it is forewarned. However, perhaps Rav Zevid retracted that [statement] below, as [the Gemara] objects to it there; for if you do not say so, that [passage] at the beginning of our tractate (2b) would be difficult for him.
